record.title: Gyárfás–Lehel–Bollobás $K$-$T$ conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n\geq 3$, and for each $1\leq k\leq n$ let $T_k$ be a tree on $k$ vertices, with the trees mutually vertex disjoint. Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices. **$K$-$T$ conjecture.** The complete graph $K_n$ can be decomposed into $n$ mutually edge-disjoint trees $H_k$, 
$$
K_n=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}H_k,
$$
 such that $T_k\cong H_k$ whenever $1\leq k\leq n$; this case is written as $\langle T_1,T_2,\dots,T_n\mid K_n\rangle$. The conjecture concerns decomposing a complete graph into prescribed tree isomorphism types; the source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Fei Ma and Bing Yao, “Topological Structures of Sets and their Subsets”, arXiv:2503.20167 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20167

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

record.title: Erdős's reverse Littlewood–Offord conjecture
record.statement:
Let $x_1,\dotsc,x_n$ be unit complex numbers, and let $\varepsilon_1,\dotsc,\varepsilon_n\in\{-1,+1\}$. **Erdős's conjecture.** The number of sums

$$
\sum_{i=1}^n \varepsilon_i x_i
$$

with

$$
\left|\sum_{i=1}^n \varepsilon_i x_i\right|\leq 1
$$

is greater than $c2^n/n$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. This conjecture is false as stated: taking an odd number of copies of $(1,0)$ and of $(0,1)$ makes every sum have norm at least $\sqrt{2}$, so the unit-radius claim cannot hold in general.
record.source_name: Lawrence Hollom, Julien Portier and Victor Souza, “Double-jump phase transition for the reverse Littlewood–Offord problem”, arXiv:2503.24202 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.24202

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2025). “It turns out that is false as stated, which can be seen in $\RR^2$ by taking an odd number of copies of $(1,0)$ and of $(0,1)$.”

record.title: Sidorenko-gap conjecture for odd linear cycles
record.statement:
For an $r$-uniform linear cycle $C^r_{2\ell+1}$ of odd length $2\ell+1$, let $s(C^r_{2\ell+1})$ denote its Sidorenko gap. **Odd linear-cycle Sidorenko-gap conjecture.** For $r\geq 3$ and $\ell\geq 2$,

$$
s(C^r_{2\ell+1})=\frac{1}{(r-1)\ell-1}.
$$

The paper proves an upper bound on this gap and gives a conditional lower bound, so the asserted equality remains open and would require a matching upper bound.
record.source_name: Lirong Deng, Jie Han, Jiaxi Nie and Sam Spiro, “Supersaturation of odd linear cycles”, arXiv:2504.05116 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05116

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

record.title: Abreu–Diwan–Jackson–Labbate–Schwenk's classification conjecture for 3-edge-connected pseudo 2-factor isomorphic graphs
record.statement:
A graph is **pseudo 2-factor isomorphic** if all of its 2-factors have the same parity of number of cycles. A **star product** is the cubic graph operation that deletes one degree-3 vertex from each factor and joins the three resulting pairs of neighbours. Let $G$ be a 3-edge-connected cubic bipartite graph.

**Abreu–Diwan–Jackson–Labbate–Schwenk's conjecture.** $G$ is pseudo 2-factor isomorphic if and only if $G$ can be obtained from $K_{3,3}$, the Heawood graph or the Pappus graph by repeated star products.

This conjecture gives a proposed classification of all 3-edge-connected cubic bipartite graphs with the parity property. The supplied text gives no resolution of this statement.
record.source_name: Marien Abreu, Jan Goedgebeur, Jorik Jooken, Federico Romaniello and Tibo Van den Eede, “The Gray graph is pseudo 2-factor isomorphic”, arXiv:2504.12095 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.12095

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2025). “This conjecture was disproved by Goedgebeur [Discr.\ Appl.\ Math.\ 193 (2015) 57--60] who constructed a counterexample $\mathcal{G}$ (of girth 6) on 30 vertices.”

record.title: Uniqueness of 2-full words modulo plane symmetries and hook-snake flips
record.statement:
Let $h>w\geq 5$ with $h\equiv_3 w$, and let $W\in\mathcal{MW}^{\leq 2}_{h\times w}$ be a 2-full word, meaning a maximal 2-dimensional binary word of degree at most $2$ in an $h\times w$ rectangle. The allowed equivalences are symmetries of the plane together with a local symmetry, namely a flip, on hook snakes.

**Uniqueness conjecture for 2-full words.** The 2-full words $W\in\mathcal{MW}^{\leq 2}_{h\times w}$ are unique up to symmetries of the plane and a local symmetry (a flip) on hook snakes.

The question concerns the exact structure of maximal bounded-degree binary words. The supplied status evidence states that this uniqueness question is open; the paper's main theorem gives bounds for maximal snakes but does not settle their exact length in terms of $h$ and $w$.
record.source_name: Alexandre Blondin Massé, Alain Goupil, Ralphael L'Heureux and Louis Marin, “Maximal 2-dimensional binary words of bounded degree”, arXiv:2505.13640 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.13640

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2025). “Thanks to Theorem , the length of maximal snakes in a $h\times w$ rectangle can be given upper and lower bounds but the question of finding their exact length in terms of $h$ and $w$ is open.”

record.title: The chromatic lower-bound conjecture for the Colin de Verdière parameter
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\chi(G)$ denote its chromatic number, and let $\nu(G)$ denote the positive semidefinite Colin de Verdière parameter.

**Chromatic lower-bound conjecture.** For any graph $G$,

$$
\nu(G)\geq \chi(G)-1.
$$

This would follow from either the $\delta$-conjecture or Hadwiger's conjecture, since the source explains that each would imply the required lower bound. The inequality is stated as open in the source; current results supplied there give only a weaker bound proportional to $\chi(G)$.
record.source_name: Francesco Barioli, Shaun M. Fallat, Himanshu Gupta and Zhongshan Li, “The Weak Version of the Graph Complement Conjecture and Partial Results for the Delta Conjecture”, arXiv:2505.24577 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24577

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

record.title: Ding and Marshall's minor conjecture for 3-connected non-Hamiltonian graphs
record.statement: Let $G$) be a 3-connected non-Hamiltonian graph. Let $K_{3,4}$ be the complete bipartite graph, let $\mathfrak{Q}^+$ be obtained from the cube by adding a new vertex adjacent to three independent vertices, and let $\mathfrak{H}$ denote the Herschel graph. **Ding and Marshall's conjecture.** Every $3$-connected non-Hamiltonian graph contains a minor of $K_{3,4}$, $\mathfrak{Q}^+$, or $\mathfrak{H}$. This conjecture concerns the characterization of minor-minimal 3-connected non-Hamiltonian graphs; the paper states that the analogous characterization problem for 4-connected graphs remains open.
record.source_name: On-Hei Solomon Lo, “On minors of non-hamiltonian graphs”, arXiv:2506.20087 (2025).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2506.20086](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20086).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20087

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2025). “It remains an open question how to characterize minor-minimal 4-connected non-hamiltonian graphs.”

record.title: The $K_7^{=}$ extremal minor conjecture for 5-connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a **5-connected graph**, meaning that deleting fewer than five vertices leaves it connected. Let $K_7^{=}$ be the graph obtained from $K_7$ by deleting two edges.

**$K_7^{=}$ extremal minor conjecture.** Every $5$-connected graph $G$ with

$$
|E(G)|\geq 4|V(G)|-9
$$

has a $K_7^{=}$-minor, unless $G\simeq K_6$.

The source presents this as a possible higher-connectivity analogue of an extremal result needed for the preceding coloring conjecture. It is not asserted as proved and is therefore open.
record.source_name: Sergey Norin and Agnes Totschnig, “Every graph with no K_7^-minor is 6-colorable”, arXiv:2507.03244 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.03244

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2025).

record.title: Steiner Tree complexity dichotomy for 1-colorful minor-closed classes
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a $1$-colorful minor-closed class, meaning a class of $1$-colorful graphs closed under taking colorful minors. A **$1$-colorful rainbow $(k\times k)$-grid** is the specified $1$-colorful rainbow grid of side length $k$ in the source. **Steiner Tree complexity dichotomy conjecture.** Unless $\mathsf{P}\neq\mathsf{NP}$, \textsc{Steiner Tree} can be solved in polynomial time in $\mathcal{C}$ if and only if there is some $k$ such that $\mathcal{C}$ excludes the $1$-colorful rainbow $(k\times k)$-grid as a colorful minor.

This conjecture proposes a sharp polynomial-time tractability dichotomy for \textsc{Steiner Tree} on $1$-colorful minor-closed classes, refining the bidimensionality-frontier discussion. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Evangelos Protopapas, Dimitrios M. Thilikos and Sebastian Wiederrecht, “Colorful Minors”, arXiv:2507.10467 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.10467

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2025).

record.title: Mohammadian's reduced-graph inertia conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a non-negative integer, and let a **reduced graph** be a graph with no redundant vertices in the sense used for reduced graphs in the paper. **Mohammadian's conjecture.** The order of every reduced graph with exactly $k$ negative eigenvalues is at most

$$
2^{k+1}-2.
$$

The paper states that this bound is tight for a construction of reduced graphs due to Kotlov and Lovász. It is cited as a conjecture proposed by Mohammadian, and no resolution is given.
record.source_name: Saieed Akbari, Clive Elphick, Hitesh Kumar, Shivaramakrishna Pragada and Quanyu Tang, “A new conjecture on the inertia of graphs”, arXiv:2508.01163 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01163

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).

record.title: Li–Feng–Peng conjecture on triangular edges in Nosal graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges. It is **Nosal** when $\lambda(G)>\sqrt{m}$. An edge is **triangular** if it is contained in a triangle.

**Li–Feng–Peng conjecture.** Every $m$-edge Nosal graph has at least $\sqrt{m}$ triangular edges.

This conjecture is presented as a spectral analogue of the Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau theorem on triangular edges. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Yongtao Li, Hong Liu and Shengtong Zhang, “More on Nosal's spectral theorem: Books and 4-cycles”, arXiv:2508.14366 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.14366

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2025).

record.title: Erdős's balanced blow-up conjecture for 5-cycles
record.statement: For $n\geq5$, consider the **balanced blow-up** of the $5$-cycle $C_5$, obtained by replacing each vertex of $C_5$ by an independent set of size $\lfloor n/5\rfloor$ or $\lceil n/5\rceil$, and each edge by a complete bipartite graph between the corresponding sets. **Erdős's conjecture.** This balanced blow-up maximizes the number of $5$-cycles among all triangle-free graphs of order $n$. The claim is an extremal refinement of the preceding bound; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Jorik Jooken, “Computer-assisted graph theory: a survey”, arXiv:2508.20825 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20825

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).

record.title: Duchet–Meyniel minor conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, and let $\alpha(G)$ denote its independence number. A **minor** of $G$ is a graph obtained from a subgraph of $G$ by contracting edges.

**Duchet–Meyniel conjecture.** Every graph $G$ of order $n$ has a $K_{\lceil n/\alpha(G)\rceil}$ minor.

This is presented as a weaker consequence of Hadwiger's conjecture. The source gives no separate resolution status for this formulation.
record.source_name: Yuqing Ji, Yue Wang, Yujun Yang and Xia Zhang, “Odd clique minors and chromatic bounds of 3K_1, paraglider-free graphs”, arXiv:2509.00929 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.00929

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).

record.title: Minimal signed Gyárfás–Sumner sets containing a negative edge
record.statement:
Let a finite set of signed graphs be a GS set when its forbidden induced-subgraph class has bounded balanced chromatic number, and call it minimal if no proper subset is a GS set. **Minimal-set conjecture.** Any minimal finite GS set containing $\widehat{(K_2,-)}$ has exactly three elements.

This statement is the signed formulation of the classical Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture for the hereditary class corresponding to graphs with no negative simple edge. The paper presents it as an open conjectural description of minimal finite GS sets.
record.source_name: Guillaume Aubian, Allen Ibiapina, Luis Kuffner, Reza Naserasr, Cyril Pujol, Cléophée Robin and Huan Zhou, “Extension of the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture to signed graphs”, arXiv:2511.03335 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.03335

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

record.title: Second covering allocation conjecture for Young diagrams
record.statement:
Let $Y$ be a Young diagram and let $H(Y)$ be the associated 3-partite 3-uniform hypergraph. Write $|Y|$ for the number of cells of $Y$, let $\tau^{(2)}(H(Y))$ denote its second covering number, and let an **allocation** be the coarse filling notion used in the paper. **Second covering allocation conjecture.** If

$$
\tau^{(2)}(H(Y))=|Y|,
$$

then $Y$ has an allocation. The paper states that this is equivalent to the Wide Partition Conjecture and the allocation conjecture. A weaker covering-number equality is known for wide diagrams, but the implication to an allocation remains open.
record.source_name: Jack Allsop, Daniel Kotlar and Ian Wanless, “Outline Rectangles, Allocations, and Latin Young Diagrams”, arXiv:2511.10548 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.10548

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2025). “Handling this problem for general matroids is hard, since even the `easy' case in which all rows of the given Young diagram have the same length is a notorious open problem known as Rota's basis conjecture .”

record.title: The rainbow version of Rosa's graceful tree conjecture
record.statement: For $X\subseteq\mathbb{N}$, let $K_X$ be the complete graph on vertex set $X$ in which each edge $ij$ has colour $|i-j|$. Write $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$. A copy of a tree in this edge-coloured graph is **rainbow** if all its edges receive distinct colours. **Rainbow version of Rosa's graceful tree conjecture.** $K_{[n]}$ contains a rainbow copy of every $n$-vertex tree $T$. This is equivalent to the graceful tree conjecture: an injective map from the vertices of $T$ into $[n]$ gives an embedding in $K_{[n]}$, and the embedding is rainbow exactly when the map is a graceful labelling. Thus the statement is a reformulation rather than a separate conjecture.
record.source_name: Shoham Letzter, Alexey Pokrovskiy and Ella Williams, “On the gracesize of trees”, arXiv:2511.11331 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.11331

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

record.title: Seymour's half-order matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, and let a **model** consist of pairwise vertex-disjoint connected branch sets, with adjacent branch sets joined by an edge. **Seymour's half-order matching conjecture.** Every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)=2$ has a 
$$
K_{\lceil |V(G)|/2\rceil}
$$
-model in which each branch set has size at most $2$. The paper presents this as an implication of Seymour's matching strengthening and later establishes equivalence, while the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Jofre Costa, Eric Luu, David R. Wood and Jung Hon Yip, “Verifying Hadwiger's Conjecture for Examples of Graphs with α(G) = 2”, arXiv:2512.17114 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17114

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

record.title: Frankl–Kupavskii conjecture for the Erdős–Kleitman problem
record.statement:
For integers $n\ge s\ge2$, define

$$
e(n,s)=\max\{ |\mathcal F|:\mathcal F\subseteq2^{[n]}\text{ and }\nu(\mathcal F)<s\}.
$$

For integers $m\ge1$ and $1\le\ell\le\lceil s/2\rceil$, set $n=(m+1)s-\ell$ and, for any $L\in\binom{[n]}{\ell-1}$, define

$$
P(m,s,\ell;L)=\{A\subseteq[n]: |A|+|A\cap L|\ge m+1\},
$$

and write $|P(m,s,\ell)|$ for its size. **Frankl–Kupavskii conjecture.** Under these assumptions,

$$
e(n,s)=|P(m,s,\ell)|.
$$

The family $P(m,s,\ell;L)$ supplies a natural lower bound because it has no $s$ pairwise disjoint members. The conjecture remains open in the stated range, with $m=3$ identified as the first unresolved value in the conjectured range.
record.source_name: Cheng Chi and Yan Wang, “A solution to Frankl and Kupavskii's conjecture concerning Erdős-Kleitman matching problem”, arXiv:2605.06389 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06389

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2026). “Despite this substantial progress, the full conjecture remains open for every $k\ge4$.”

record.title: Efficient sampling conjecture for Potts models on random regular bipartite graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a random $\Delta$-regular bipartite graph on $2n$ vertices, let $\mu_{G,q;\beta}$ be the anti-ferromagnetic $q$-state Potts Gibbs distribution, and let an FPAUS mean a fully polynomial-time almost-uniform sampler. **Efficient-sampling conjecture.** For $\beta>0$, with high probability there exists an FPAUS for $\mu_{G,q;\beta}$ running in time polynomial in $n$ and $\Delta$. Although single-site Glauber dynamics can mix torpidly, whether another fast Markov chain, such as polymer dynamics, yields an FPAUS remains open.
record.source_name: Zhidan Li, Siyu Liu and Kuan Yang, “Counting and Sampling Anti-ferromagnetic Potts Models on Random Regular Bipartite Graphs in the Non-uniqueness Regime”, arXiv:2606.21250 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21250

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2026). “On the other side, in spite of the torpid mixing of $P^{\GD}$, it remains open whether there exists a fast Markov chain to design an $\FPAUS$ for $\mu_{G, q; \beta}$ (for example, polymer dynamics in ).”

record.title: The cycle double cover conjecture for bridgeless cubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. A **cycle double cover** (CyDC) is a collection of cycles in which every edge of $G$ belongs to exactly two cycles; equivalently, a circuit double cover (CiDC) is a finite family of connected $2$-regular subgraphs with the same property.

**Szekeres–Seymour conjecture.** Every bridgeless cubic graph has a CyDC, equivalently a CiDC.

The conjecture is a central existence problem about cycle and circuit coverings of graphs. The source states that it was recently proven by OpenAI, although the proof had not yet appeared in a refereed publication and was accompanied by a Lean formalization.
record.source_name: Radek Hušek and Robert Šámal, “Exponentially Many Circuit Double Covers”, arXiv:2607.24724 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24724

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of July 2026); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)
